def: A structured review conducted after a mission to assess what happened, what worked, and what needs improvement.
The designated geographic area where a military operation is being conducted.
Term used to indicate urgency. Act or report immediately.
Evaluation of damage caused to a target following a strike or engagement.
Friendly forces. Used in OPFOR/BLUFOR designations to distinguish allies from enemies.
A defensive position from which a unit can engage the enemy.
Air action against hostile targets that are in close proximity to friendly forces.
The officer in command of a unit or element during an operation.
Either the headquarters location for a command element, or a designated point on a route to be secured.
Combat conducted at very close range, typically inside buildings or confined spaces.
Expected time for a unit or element to reach a destination.
The process of withdrawing from an area after completing a mission.
An abbreviated form of an operations order used to make changes to a mission in progress.
A secured forward position used to support tactical operations.
An enemy target of significant importance whose capture or neutralisation would severely impact enemy operations.
The process of moving into an operational area without being detected.
A designated starting point for beginning an attack or navigation phase.
A combatant who has died as a result of hostile action.
A designated area where aircraft can land to insert or extract personnel.
A combatant whose status is unknown following hostile engagement.
Level of protection worn against chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear threats.
A position from which military observations are made.
Enemy or hostile forces in a given scenario.
A directive issued by a commander to subordinates for the purpose of executing an operation.
A covered and concealed location near the objective where final preparations are made before an assault.
Confirmed identification of a target as hostile before engagement.
A line used for control and coordination, often named and used to track progress of an advance.
An enemy combatant captured and held according to rules of engagement.
A unit held on standby to respond rapidly to unexpected threats or situations.
Directives that define the circumstances and limitations under which forces may engage.
A designated location where elements regroup following dispersion or contact with the enemy.
A pre-arranged meeting point for two or more units.
A verbal or written update on the current status of a unit, area, or operation.
A set of step-by-step instructions compiled to carry out routine operations.
Radio code indicating that a unit is actively engaged with the enemy.
A combatant who has been injured as a result of hostile action.
A reference point in physical space used for navigation or coordination.
The military arm and primary government body of humanity in the Halo universe.
The intelligence and special operations division of the UNSC. Operates in extreme secrecy.
Elite UNSC shock infantry who deploy from orbit in Single Occupant Exoatmospheric Insertion Vehicles (SOEIVs).
The primary offensive weapon of UNSC warships, firing ferric tungsten slugs at high velocity.
Commonly called a drop pod. Used by ODSTs for orbital insertion into combat zones.
The powered exoskeleton armour system used by UNSC Spartan supersoldiers.
UNSC smart or dumb AI constructs used to support warship operations, tactics, and logistics.
Standard UNSC anti-materiel sniper rifle. 14.5×114mm semi-automatic.
UNSC standard-issue assault rifle series. Chambered in 7.62×51mm full-auto configuration.
Standard UNSC sidearm series. Semi-automatic, 12.7×40mm.
An ongoing rebel movement against the UNSC, primarily operating in the Outer Colonies. The 505th's primary OPFOR.
Colloquial term for members of the Insurrectionist movement.
UNSC interceptor and strike craft used for space superiority and planetary bombing runs.
The primary UNSC dropship and atmospheric combat craft. Used for troop insertion and extraction.
UNSC's iconic light utility vehicle. Available in multiple variants including LRV and LAAV.
The ACE3 mod framework adding realistic medical, explosives, interactions, and ballistics to Arma 3.
A required Arma 3 framework mod providing shared functionality for most other mods to work correctly.
A mod adding realistic radio simulation including range limits, terrain effects, and interference.
Default ACE keybind to raise hands and surrender.
An alternative radio mod to ACRE2. Provides voice comms tied to in-game radios.
Arma 3's built-in real-time mission editor allowing a GM to control the mission dynamically.
A player joining a mission that is already underway.
Arma 3's loadout editor, accessible in-game via ACE interact or scripted triggers.
The primary Arma 3 mod the 505th uses, adding UNSC/Halo assets, weapons, vehicles, and factions.
Build tool used by the 505th developer team to compile and package the aux mod.
The 505th's custom Arma 3 mod adding unit-specific content layered on top of OPTRE.
Radio term indicating a pause between messages, or used to interrupt a transmission in an emergency.
A unique identifier used in radio communications to identify a unit, vehicle, or individual.
General term for radio or verbal communication between elements.
A specific radio frequency or channel assigned to a unit or mission.
Radio proword indicating transmission is complete and a reply is expected.
Radio proword indicating the conversation is complete and no reply is expected.
Radio proword confirming a message has been received and understood.
Radio proword meaning the message is understood and the instruction will be followed.
The command element or HQ on the radio net.
A designated area where casualties are brought for treatment and stabilisation prior to evacuation.
The movement of casualties from the point of injury to medical treatment facilities.
Evacuation of casualties by dedicated medical assets, typically aircraft.
ACE3 medical item for basic self-treatment. Limited to bandaging in standard configs.
ACE3 medical item for treating wounds on other players. More versatile than a PAK.
ACE3 advanced medical item required for surgical and IV procedures. Corpsman use.
Informal term for a casualty requiring medical attention.
Highest priority casualty — life-threatening injury requiring immediate treatment.
Moderate priority — serious injury but can wait for treatment without immediate risk of death.
Minor injuries. Can walk and wait for treatment.
ACE3 medical item used to stop bleeding on limbs. Must be removed to restore circulation.
